# healthchecksio_check (Resource)

A check. The check is simple when it has `timeout`, and cron or OnCalendar when it has `schedule`. Each attribute has the name of its API field.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "healthchecksio_channels" "email" {
  kind = "email"
}

# A simple check: one ping each hour, and a grace period of 10 minutes.
resource "healthchecksio_check" "backup" {
  name     = "Nightly backup"
  slug     = "nightly-backup"
  tags     = ["backup", "prod"]
  timeout  = 3600
  grace    = 600
  channels = data.healthchecksio_channels.email.ids
}

# A cron check: one ping at minute 42 of each hour (UTC), and a grace period of 3 hours.
resource "healthchecksio_check" "sync" {
  name     = "Mirror sync"
  slug     = "mirror-sync"
  schedule = "42 * * * *"
  tz       = "UTC"
  grace    = 10800
  channels = data.healthchecksio_channels.email.ids
}

# An OnCalendar check that accepts only POST pings, and fails a ping that does not
# contain "Backup successful".
resource "healthchecksio_check" "report" {
  name                = "Monthly report"
  schedule            = "*-*~1 12:00"
  methods             = "POST"
  success_kw          = ["Backup successful"]
  filter_http_body    = true
  filter_default_fail = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the check.

### Optional

- `channels` (Set of String) The UUIDs of the integrations that get the alerts of the check. Get them from `healthchecksio_channels`. An empty set removes all integrations. If you do not set this attribute, the provider does not change the integrations of the check.
- `desc` (String) The description of the check.
- `failure_kw` (Set of String) The keywords that make a ping a failure signal. Use them with the `filter_*` attributes. A keyword cannot contain a comma.
- `filter_body` (Boolean) Look for the keywords in the body of an email ping.
- `filter_default_fail` (Boolean) If true, a filtered ping that has no keyword is a failure signal. If false, the server ignores that ping.
- `filter_http_body` (Boolean) Look for the keywords in the body of an HTTP ping.
- `filter_subject` (Boolean) Look for the keywords in the subject of an email ping.
- `grace` (Number) The grace period in seconds: the time after a late ping before the check is down.
- `manual_resume` (Boolean) If true, a paused check ignores pings and stays paused until you resume it. If false, a ping resumes the check.
- `methods` (String) The HTTP methods for pings: `""` accepts HEAD, GET and POST, and `"POST"` accepts only POST.
- `schedule` (String) For a cron or OnCalendar check: the cron or systemd OnCalendar expression. The server finds the type of the expression.
- `slug` (String) The slug of the check, for a ping URL with the ping key of the project. The API does not make it from the name.
- `start_kw` (Set of String) The keywords that make a ping a start signal. Use them with the `filter_*` attributes. A keyword cannot contain a comma.
- `success_kw` (Set of String) The keywords that make a ping a success signal. Use them with the `filter_*` attributes. A keyword cannot contain a comma.
- `tags` (Set of String) The tags of the check. A tag cannot contain a space.
- `timeout` (Number) For a simple check: the expected period between pings, in seconds. If the check has no `schedule` and you do not set it, the value is 86400. It is null for a check with a `schedule`.
- `tz` (String) For a check with a `schedule`: the IANA time zone of the schedule. The default is `UTC`. Use the canonical name. If you give a legacy name (for example `Europe/Kiev`), the server stores the canonical name (`Europe/Kyiv`), the apply fails, and the error gives the name to use.

### Read-Only

- `badge_url` (String) The URL of the 2-state SVG badge of the check. For a JSON or Shields badge, change the extension to `.json` or `.shields`. For a 3-state badge, change `/b/2/` to `/b/3/`.
- `id` (String) The unique_key of the check: 40 hex digits. Use it to import the check. It is not a ping credential.
- `ping_url` (String, Sensitive) The ping URL. It contains the UUID.
- `uuid` (String, Sensitive) The UUID of the check. It is the ping credential.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = healthchecksio_check.backup
  identity = {
    unique_key = "a6c7b0a8a66bed0df66abfdab3c77736861703ee"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `unique_key` (String) The unique_key of the check: 40 hex digits. It is not a ping credential.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The id is the unique_key of the check. You can keep this block in git.
import {
  to = healthchecksio_check.backup
  id = "a6c7b0a8a66bed0df66abfdab3c77736861703ee"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the unique_key. The unique_key is not a ping credential.
terraform import healthchecksio_check.backup a6c7b0a8a66bed0df66abfdab3c77736861703ee

# Import with the UUID. The UUID is the ping credential. Do not put it in a file in git.
terraform import healthchecksio_check.backup 31365bce-8da9-4729-8ff3-aaa71d56b712
```
